successors.note: 655: 'Western Guo was destroyed by the Duke Xian of Jin' (page). The jin dossier of ea-01-b carries a catch-all gain of Western Guo and four other Shanxi states at 676, not 655.

capitals.name: Shangyang (Sanmenxia)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Yong (雍地) Sanmenxia'; after moving east 'eventually migrating to today Sanmenxia', a new capital 'built at Shangyang (上阳) straddling both banks of the Yellow River'. The earlier seat at Yong is not located and the move is undated, so one dot at Sanmenxia stands for the whole span.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Western Guo). Infobox Established 1046 BC, 'Disestablished: 687 BC'; 'in the Yellow River valley between Xi'an and Luoyang'; no area. The 45 km disc south-west of Sanmenxia is a stand-in, kept clear of the Yu disc to the north.

region.text: Western Guo, 'in the Yellow River valley between Xi'an and Luoyang', capital Shangyang 'straddling both banks of the Yellow River' at Sanmenxia (list page: from north-eastern Pinglu County, Shanxi, and Sanmenxia to Lingbao)

ledger.note: 1046: King Wu enfeoffs his uncle Guo Shu. Infobox 'Established: 1046 BC'; 'his uncle Guo Shu received grants of land at Yong' after King Wu destroyed the Shang. The Yong site is not located (the footnote says 'Modern day Pinglu County, Shanxi Province' for Guo Shu), so the region is the state's later Sanmenxia seat.

region.text: Western Guo, 'in the Yellow River valley between Xi'an and Luoyang', capital Shangyang 'straddling both banks of the Yellow River' at Sanmenxia (list page: from north-eastern Pinglu County, Shanxi, and Sanmenxia to Lingbao)

ledger.note: 655: Jin destroys Western Guo. 'In 655 BCE, Western Guo was destroyed by the Duke Xian of Jin'; Jin first asked leave of Yu to cross its land, and 'After conquering Guo it conquered Yu'.

ledger.note: 655: the state of Western Guo ends in Jin's conquest; 'The Guo leader Guo Gong Chou fled to the Zhou capital Luoyang'. The infobox's 687 BC is the Qin extinction of Xiao Guo in the text, not this state.

Yu, Pinglu County near Xia County, Shanxi (List of Zhou dynasty states)

wars.outcome: Jin borrowed a road through Yu to destroy Western Guo in 655 BC and then conquered Yu (the 'borrowing a road to conquer Guo' stratagem).
wars.note: The infobox says 'Disestablished: 687 BC' but the text puts the destruction in 655 (and says Qin wiped out 'Xiao Guo' in 687); 655 is used, with the list page's '1046-655 BCE, Jin'.

certainty.note: No Guo boundary is on the page; the move east is undated. Soft throughout.

sources.title: Western Guo
sources.note: Infobox (1046 BC to 687 BC, capital Yong/Sanmenxia); Guo Shu's grant; move east before the Quanrong; Shangyang; 655 BC Jin conquest and the borrowed road through Yu.

sources.title: List of Zhou dynasty states
sources.note: Table rows Western Guo (西虢國/南虢國): 1046-655 BCE, Jin, Pinglu County to Lingbao; Yu (虞國): 1046-655, Jin, Pinglu County near Xia County; Eastern Guo: 1046-767, Zheng, Xingyang; Northern Guo: ?-655, Jin.

notes: Pages opened (2 of 1-2): Western Guo, List of Zhou dynasty states. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). The page title is Western Guo; the list distinguishes Western/Southern Guo (Sanmenxia), Northern Guo (Pinglu, also destroyed by Jin in 655) and Eastern Guo (Xingyang, Zheng 767; the zheng dossier of ea-01-d carries it without a location): only the first is a dossier here. DATES: infobox disestablished 687 BC conflicts with the page's own 655 conquest; 655 is used (confidence 3 for the event, region 2). The eastward move 'due to harassment and invasion by the Quanrong tribes' is undated, so no capital_move or gain is written. REGION: Sanmenxia and Shangyang are not gazetteer places (coordinates used). AREA: none on the pages. No rulers (the page lists only Guo Shu and Guo Zhong). The jin dossier dates its Shanxi small-state gains to 676; the pages opened here give 655 for Guo and Yu.
